context: Current closing price of DuPont (DD): $48.19 USD as of 2026-06-22.
justification_text:
At the one-day horizon, the point estimate of 48.35 was anchored heavily to the last observed price or level, with only modest drift expected over such a short window. Short-term momentum, intraday mean-reversion tendencies, and the absence of any immediately scheduled major catalysts all supported a forecast very close to the current reading. The tight 90% confidence interval of 46.8 to 49.9 reflects that over a single trading session, realized volatility tends to be constrained, and large gaps are relatively rare absent a specific shock. Essentially, the one-day forecast is dominated by the prior level with a small noise term layered on top.

At the one-week horizon, the point estimate of 48.6 reflects a slight upward drift assumption, perhaps consistent with a mild bullish bias in the underlying trend or a modest mean-reversion pull if the asset had recently dipped. The wider confidence interval of 45.5 to 51.7 acknowledges that over five trading sessions, news flow, positioning shifts, and macro data releases can meaningfully move prices. Weekly intervals also capture the possibility of gap opens, sentiment shifts, and liquidity variations across different days of the week, all of which add variance that a single-day forecast can largely ignore.

The one-month point estimate of 49.5 incorporates a continuation of the mild upward drift while the confidence interval of 42.0 to 57.0 is substantially wider, reflecting compounding uncertainty over roughly twenty trading sessions. At this horizon, a much broader range of outcomes becomes plausible — central bank decisions, earnings releases, geopolitical developments, or shifts in broader market risk appetite could each independently move the needle by several points.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside even these wider intervals include a sudden liquidity crisis or flash crash compressing prices well below 42, an unexpected policy announcement or surprise macro data print causing a sharp gap move, or a broader risk-on rally driven by coordinated central bank easing that could push toward or beyond 57. Structural breaks — such as a regime change in volatility or a correlation breakdown with related assets — represent tail risks that are by definition underweighted in any historically calibrated interval, meaning realized outcomes in genuinely unusual environments could easily fall outside the stated bounds.
